text:
morgan: quick heads-up — i'm opening a rollout for a small runtime config gate: route_by_quota. need ops handoff + console UX safety-nudge ideas. filing the gate as dry-run first.

jia: thanks. can you paste the exact payload? want to validate telemetry tags so dashboard picks it up.

morgan: sure — here's the draft gate we're using (dry-run):
```json
{
  "flag": "route_by_quota",
  "enabled": true,
  "quota_pct": 0.02,
  "min_tokens": 10,
  "fallback_model": "rwd-small-v2",
  "dry_run": true,
  "tags": ["release/2026-03-config-gates", "telemetry:route_by_quota"]
}
```

sam: small nit — quota_pct should be a string in the runtime API v2, otherwise previous parsers choke. we had this with the last rollout.

morgan: good catch. i'll stringify it. we also need to ensure client SDKs don't treat this as feature-flagging semantics; this is traffic routing.

leo: from ops side: handoff checklist please. what telemetry will we surface? latency by model, error rate, quota-utilization, and a per-route sample of request ids for quick investigations. also a kill-switch.

emily: ux idea: show a safety nudge in the console when someone increases quota_pct above 1% — small modal that highlights "expected cost delta" and links to a dry-run. we can auto-populate sample cost numbers using the route's token distribution.

praveen: +1. also suggest an inline dry-run button next to the toggle that executes the runtime dry-run path and returns a small report: hit-rate, predicted token increase, and top-3 impacted clients.

jia: telemetry naming: please add `gate.name`, `gate.version`, `gate.phase` (dry-run/canary/active) to every event. that makes dashboards and alerts trivial to wire.

morgan: noted. i'll add `gate.phase` and `gate.version` to the payload. quick API debate: should `dry_run` be a first-class bool on the gate object, or a top-level rollout parameter?

sam: prefer top-level rollout param because it lets multiple gates be tested in one rollout bundle without mutating the flags themselves. also preserves a clear audit trail.

leo: ops prefers first-class on the gate so we can store state and see which gates were created as dry-run historically. audit log folks care about that.

emily: UX tradeoff — top-level makes the UI easier for multi-flag rollouts; first-class makes gate details obvious. Maybe both: default to top-level rollout.dry_run but allow gate-level override.

praveen: implementation cost? adding two places for dry_run raises validation complexity but seems doable. need to finalise schema v2.

morgan: ok — proposal: rollout object with `dry_run` (default), and gate object `dry_run_override` (nullable). validators: if gate.dry_run_override === false && rollout.dry_run === true, we need explicit confirmation in console.

sam: make that confirmation require typing the gate name. scope creep but reduces accidental activations.

oncall-bot: Deploy scheduled: config-apply job #3621 queued to canary pool at 03:15 UTC :robot_face: 

leo: ops checklist (copyable):
- confirm telemetry tags exist and show up in staging dashboards
- dry-run CLI test: `/config apply --file gate.json --dry-run --audit-note "canary test"`
- create canary alert: gate.phase=="canary" AND (latency_p95 > baseline * 1.2 OR error_rate > 0.5%) -> page oncall
- run sample-backfill to ensure historical dashboards don't N/A out
- pre-create rollback playbook (exact `config rollback --to` commands)

morgan: here is the CLI snippet i'll use for ops testing: 
```
# validate schema & dry run
/config validate gate.json
/config apply --file gate.json --dry-run --audit-note "eng-platform canary"

# when ready to promote
/config apply --file gate.json --promote --audit-note "promote to canary"
```

emily: UX microcopy suggestion for the safety nudge modal:
"You're about to route X% of traffic to a lower-cost model. This can lower latency for some customers but may change outputs. Run a dry-run to preview affected clients and expected token delta."

praveen: regarding quotas interacting with route-by-cost: we need a circuit that prevents quota bump from triggering routing until token burn thresholds are met for the route. otherwise billing surprises. basically: gating condition = quota_pct > 0 AND monthly_token_delta_estimate < budget_threshold => block.

jia: that sounds right. can we compute `monthly_token_delta_estimate` from recent 7-day token distribution? put a little `i` tooltip explaining the estimation method.

morgan: will add the tooltip and the math: `est = sum_{clients} avg_tokens_per_request * estimated_routed_requests`. keep it conservative +10%.

leo: ops request: expose a fastpath in console to temporarily freeze routing (not full rollback) that we can click during incidents. labeling: "pause routing handoff" vs "disable gate". pause should just set gate.phase=paused and keep config in place.

sam: backend note: phase transitions must be idempotent. multiple concurrent promote/pause requests are likely. add a compare-and-swap token on the rollout object.

morgan: agreed — i'll add `rollout.etag` and require it in promote/pause APIs. console will fetch latest etag.

emily: do we want an audit banner at the top of the console route page showing the last 3 actions (who, what, when)? ops likes it.

leo: yes please. also add quick links to the rollback command in the audit banner.

praveen: test plan idea: small A/B test on the safety nudge modal — half of internal users see the modal, half inline helper — measure dry-run usage and accidental promotes.

morgan: great. timeline: i'll prepare the schema PR tomorrow, will include telemetry keys and `etag` + dry_run semantics. ops, can you run the staging checklist on Wed?

leo: can do. ring oncall when you hit promote.

sam: i'll add schema unit tests and an integration test for CAS semantics.

emily: i'll mock up the modal and the pause UX tonight and drop screenshots in the thread.

morgan: thanks all. leaving the thread open for screenshots & the PR link. :thumbsup:
